headers.comment: Vite fingerprints every asset filename, so they can be cached forever. Without this they inherit the default one-hour max-age and a returning visitor re-downloads the fonts on every session.

index.html must never be cached. It is the only file that names the current bundle hashes, so a cached copy pins the browser to a deploy that no longer exists. Firebase defaults it to max-age=3600, which meant every visitor ran an hour-old app after each deploy — and I spent three deploys debugging a stale page because of it.
The SPA rewrite means any unmatched path also serves index.html, so it needs the same treatment.
